title: DHS Field Engagement Accountability Act
official_summary:
DHS Field Engagement Accountability Act

This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to develop and update at least once every five years a strategy for DHS engagement with fusion centers. The term "fusion center" means a collaborative effort of two or more government agencies that combines resources, expertise, or information to maximize the ability of such agencies to detect, prevent, investigate, apprehend, and respond to criminal or terrorist activity.

The Office of Intelligence and Analysis of DHS shall provide personnel and support to fusion centers, publish performance metrics for DHS field personnel assigned to fusion centers, and develop and implement training for fusion center personnel.

DHS intelligence and information components shall develop policies and metrics to ensure effective use of the unclassified Homeland Security Information Sharing Network and shall assess and implement enhancements to improve such network.

summary.headline: This 2020 law requires DHS to set up a strategy, training, performance metrics, and information-sharing rules for its work with state and local fusion centers.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires DHS to create a strategy for working with fusion centers, which are collaborations of two or more government agencies that share resources and information to detect and respond to criminal or terrorist activity, and to update that strategy at least every five years. DHS's Office of Intelligence and Analysis must provide staff and support to fusion centers, publish performance metrics for DHS personnel assigned there, and develop training for fusion center staff. DHS intelligence and information offices must also set policies and metrics for the unclassified Homeland Security Information Sharing Network and assess ways to improve it.

who_it_affects.how: They must receive training developed and carried out under the law.

who_it_affects.group: DHS personnel assigned to fusion centers
who_it_affects.how: Their performance will be measured against metrics that DHS must publish.

who_it_affects.group: DHS Office of Intelligence and Analysis
who_it_affects.how: It must provide personnel, support, training, and performance metrics for fusion centers.

who_it_affects.group: State, local, and tribal agencies that take part in fusion centers
who_it_affects.how: They work with DHS under the new strategy, training, and information-sharing rules, though the summary does not describe specific new duties for them.

who_it_affects.group: Users of the Homeland Security Information Sharing Network
who_it_affects.how: DHS must set policies and metrics for the network and assess improvements to it.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on March 2, 2020, but the summary does not list specific deadlines for the strategy, metrics, or training beyond the five-year update cycle.
